Airport security lines: They call it "security," but the only thing I feel secure about is the TSA agent's ability to find my keys in my ass crack.
Endless Zoom meetings: I’ve had more small talk with my laptop than actual human contact, and my laptop still judges me.
First dates: I went on a first date with a librarian — she was quiet, organized, and had a rule about talking during the movie. So I whispered, "Do you want popcorn?" She said, "Shhh, you're spoiling the silence."
Smart home devices (like a Roomba or Ale: I told my Roomba to "clean the living room," and it looked at me like, "You’re gonna have to be more specific—did you mean the floor or the *embarrassing life choices* scattered around?"
Going to the gym for the first time: I went to the gym for the first time, and the guy next to me was lifting weights with one hand while eating a burrito. I just wanted to cry, but I was too out of shape to even sit down.
Customer service phone menus: I love how customer service menus assume I have a full-time relationship with every department — "For billing issues, press 1. For technical support, press 2." Sounds like I’m dating the whole company.
Trying to eat healthy/Dieting: I tried to eat healthy this week, so I replaced my snacks with books. Turns out, "craving a chapter a day" doesn't fill you up.
The behavior of cats vs. dogs: Cats are like the bosses of the human they're living with, and the dog is just the HR department trying to keep the peace.
Self-checkout machines at the grocery st: Self-checkout machines are like the toddler of technology—supposed to be helpful, but if you blink, it's crying and needs a timeout.
Insomnia and trying to fall asleep: I tried counting sheep to fall asleep, but I kept wondering why there were so many sheep in my bedroom and where the farmer was.
Buying things you don't need online: I bought a futuristic smart mirror online that tells me I look great—turns out, it just read my credit card expiration date out loud.
Awkward family gatherings: My family’s so awkward together, we could win a reality show — the tagline would be, “No drama, just disapproval.”
Streaming service algorithms (e.g., Netf: I love how the Netflix algorithm thinks I'm a "Mystery Buff" after I watched one episode of *Sherlock* from 2009. Next thing I know, I'm getting deep into true crime documentaries at 2 a.m. All because of a *single* episode I binged while my phone was possessed.
Coffee shop baristas and complicated ord: I went to a coffee shop and ordered a "milk-based drink with espresso." The barista looked at me like I just asked for a horse.
Commuting in heavy traffic: I love how commuting in heavy traffic teaches you patience… until you see the truck in front of you eating a sandwich and you realize it’s testing your limits.
Job interviews: I went to a job interview and the whole time the manager kept saying, "But what *makes you unique?*" So I said, "I can’t wait to find out."
Keeping houseplants alive: I bought a cactus to keep me alive, but now I’m worried it’s just trying to make a point.
Forgetting passwords: I forgot my password again, so I tried "password"—still doesn’t work. Turns out, even my phone doesn’t trust me anymore.
High school reunions: I went to a high school reunion and saw my old math teacher—she asked how I’m doing. I said, "Great, I just got a 401(k) and a restraining order." She gave me an A for effort.
Assembling flat-pack furniture (e.g., IK: I bought a bookshelf from IKEA, which was just a box of wood and a diagram that looked like a modern art masterpiece. Took me three hours and a philosophy degree to assemble it. Still waiting for the part where it actually holds books.
Tech support/Helping parents with techno: I offered to help my dad set up his new phone, and halfway through I realized he didn’t need tech support—he needed therapy and a will.
Alarm clocks and waking up early: My alarm clock rings at 6 a.m. — I told it to wake me up at 7, but it’s clearly trying to make me a better version of myself.
The culture of social media influencers: I followed an influencer's 10-step skincare routine and ended up with 10 new products and a zit I can't pronounce.
Cryptocurrencies or \"Tech Bros\": Blockchain, the only chain that's holding my savings and my dignity.
Going to the dentist: I went to the dentist and he said I was brushing too hard — I said, "Well, you try scraping plaque off a set of teeth that won’t stop talking about their feelings."
Moving to a new apartment: Moving to a new apartment is like dating someone new—you hope they have good storage and don’t leave wet towels on the floor.
Annoying neighbors: I had a neighbor once who thought it was normal to yell movie lines at 2 a.m. I didn't even know *The Godfather* had a second act.
Overpacking for a vacation: I try to pack light, but my suitcase always ends up judging me. Luggage has drama I didn’t sign up for.
I swipe right on a guy on Tinder, and his bio says, "Loves travel, good food, and spontaneous road trips." I message him, "So, what's the plan for the road trip *we're* about to embark on?"
Public transportation/Subways: Subways are like emotional support elevators — you’re squished with strangers for 20 minutes and no one says a word, but somehow, you emerge a slightly different person.
Wedding planning: Wedding planning is like assembling IKEA furniture, but instead of a bookshelf, you're building a fantasy, and there's no instruction manual—and the love of your life is timing you.
Autocorrect text message fails: I tried to text "I'll be there in five," and autocorrect changed it to "I'll be their fin." So now I'm just waiting for their fin to show up.
Procrastination: I told myself I'd start organizing my life next year— turns out, I was just a one-year deadline away from a mid-life crisis.
Group chats that never stop buzzing: My group chat is like a beehive if the bees had no concept of boundaries and just buzzed 24/7 about their feelings.
The cost of living/Being broke: I used to worry about the cost of living, but now I just worry about the cost of existing — rent’s $2,000, my willpower’s $0.
Getting a bad haircut: I got a bad haircut, and now I look like I lost a game of 'let's see how long we can go without a mirror.'
Overly complicated modern fitness trends: Trying to do a plank now requires a 20-minute tutorial, a $300 smart mat, and three protein shakes. Just hold still, it’s not a TikTok algorithm.
People who talk at the movie theater: I tried to talk during the movie once, and the guy behind me shouted, "Do you want to watch the film or just give a recap?" Turns out, he was right — that's basically what I'm doing now.
Cooking disasters: I tried to make a soufflé once and it collapsed harder than my self-esteem after a bad breakup.
Small talk about the weather: I tried making small talk about the weather, but even the clouds rolled their eyes at me.
Modern fashion trends: Wearing pants that end above the ankles is now called "statement-making," which is just fashionable code for "I bought the wrong size."
Waiting in doctors' offices: I’ve learned that waiting in a doctor’s office is just society’s way of saying, “You’re not important—now wait in the land of expired magazines and sad children.”
Getting older/Turning 30: I woke up one day and realized half my friends are dead and the other half are on LinkedIn.
Video game culture: I tried to explain to my grandma that I "beat the final boss," and now she won’t stop trying to get me to fight her in chess. Checkmate, Nana — but I came to negotiate, not to blow things up.
Corporate buzzwords (e.g., \"Synergy\"): Trying to explain my job using buzzwords is like trying to build a house with only hammers and enthusiasm — it’s all synergy and no structure.
Dealing with landlords: I told my landlord his rent increase was like a horror movie — it had a slow build, a shocking revelation, and left me screaming into the void. He said I wasn't "contractually obligated" to be that dramatic.
Astrological signs/Horoscopes: I checked my horoscope this morning and it said I'd have a lucky day—turns out the "lucky" part was the only part they got right.
People who overshare online: People who overshare online are like uninvited guests who brought a PowerPoint.
Veganism or extreme dietary restrictions: I went vegan for a week and now I'm just a sad person who stares at fruit.
Trying to assemble a tent/Camping: Trying to assemble a tent is like solving a 3D puzzle... if the puzzle pieces were controlled by a sadistic child who only speaks in Ikea manuals.
